records.source: וַיְבִיאֵ֖נִי אֶל־הַהֵיכָ֑ל וַיָּ֣מָד אֶת־הָאֵילִ֗ים שֵׁשׁ־אַמּ֨וֹת רֹ֧חַב־מִפּ֛וֹ וְשֵׁשׁ־אַמּֽוֹת־רֹ֥חַב מִפּ֖וֹ רֹ֥חַב הָאֹֽהֶל׃
records.gloss: And he brought me to the temple, and he measured the jambs, six cubits breadth from here and six cubits breadth from here, [the] breadth of the tent.
pieces: Then he brought me into the main hall of the temple and measured the jambs. They were {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|six cubits}} thick on each side, the width of the tent.

L.1: Then he brought me to the hall, and he measured the jambs: six cubits wide here and six cubits wide there, the width of the tent.

R.1: Then he took me into the main room of the temple. He measured the side posts at its entrance. They were {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|six cubits}} thick on each side, the width of the tent.

decisions.choice: the hall: the main room of the temple building, the holy place
decisions.reason: The word can mean a palace or a temple as a whole, but here, as in 1 Kings 6:3, 5, 17, it is the large room between the porch and the inner room, where the lampstands and the table stood in Solomon's temple.

decisions.choice: the width of the tent: a puzzling phrase
decisions.reason: "Tent" may recall the tabernacle, whose frame was six cubits wide at the back in some reckonings, or it may be a copying slip for the word for "jamb". The Septuagint does not have it in this form. The translation keeps the received text.

decisions.choice: the hall (L); the main hall of the temple (B); the main room of the temple (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 6:3 and 6:17. The same English is used for this room through chapters 41-46.

decisions.choice: jambs (L, B); side posts (R)
decisions.reason: As in 40:9.

records.heading: The temple building

records.source: וְרֹ֣חַב הַפֶּתַח֮ עֶ֣שֶׂר אַמּוֹת֒ וְכִתְפ֣וֹת הַפֶּ֔תַח חָמֵ֤שׁ אַמּוֹת֙ מִפּ֔וֹ וְחָמֵ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת מִפּ֑וֹ וַיָּ֤מָד אָרְכּוֹ֙ אַרְבָּעִ֣ים אַמָּ֔ה וְרֹ֖חַב עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אַמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] breadth of the entrance [was] ten cubits, and [the] sides of the entrance five cubits from here and five cubits from here; and he measured its length, forty cubits, and breadth twenty cubits.
pieces: The entrance was {{units:about 17 1/2 feet|ten cubits}} wide, and the walls on either side of it were {{units:about 8 3/4 feet|five cubits}} wide. He measured the main hall: it was {{units:about 70 feet|forty cubits}} long and {{units:about 35 feet|twenty cubits}} wide.

L.2: And the entrance [was] ten cubits wide, and the sides of the entrance five cubits here and five cubits there; and he measured its length, forty cubits, and [its] width, twenty cubits.

R.2: The doorway was {{units:about 17 1/2 feet|ten cubits}} wide. The walls on each side of it were {{units:about 8 3/4 feet|five cubits}} wide. He measured the main room. It was {{units:about 70 feet|forty cubits}} long and {{units:about 35 feet|twenty cubits}} wide.

decisions.choice: forty cubits by twenty: the size of the main hall of Solomon's temple
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 6:2 and 6:17 give Solomon's main hall the same measures. Ezekiel's temple building keeps the plan of the first temple, while its courts and gates are new.

records.source: וּבָ֣א לִפְנִ֔ימָה וַיָּ֥מָד אֵֽיל־הַפֶּ֖תַח שְׁתַּ֣יִם אַמּ֑וֹת וְהַפֶּ֨תַח֙ שֵׁ֣שׁ אַמּ֔וֹת וְרֹ֥חַב הַפֶּ֖תַח שֶׁ֥בַע אַמּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: And he went within and measured [the] jamb of the entrance, two cubits, and the entrance six cubits, and [the] breadth of the entrance seven cubits.
pieces: Then he went into the inner room and measured the jambs of its entrance: they were {{units:about 3 1/2 feet|two cubits}} thick. The entrance was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|six cubits}} wide, and its side walls were {{units:about 12 1/4 feet|seven cubits}} wide.

L.3: Then he went inside and measured the entrance's jamb, two cubits, and the entrance, six cubits, and the entrance's breadth, seven cubits.

R.3: Then he went on into the inner room. He measured the side posts of its doorway. They were {{units:about 3 1/2 feet|two cubits}} thick. The doorway was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|six cubits}} wide, and the walls on each side of it were {{units:about 12 1/4 feet|seven cubits}} wide.

decisions.choice: he went inside: the man enters the inner room alone
decisions.reason: Ezekiel is brought into the main hall (verse 1), but the guide goes on into the inner room by himself. Only the high priest could enter the most holy place, once a year (Leviticus 16:2, 34), and Ezekiel, though a priest, does not follow.

decisions.choice: the entrance six cubits, and the breadth of the entrance seven: the opening and the walls beside it
decisions.reason: Six cubits is the width of the doorway; seven cubits is usually taken as the width of the wall on each side of it, as in verse 2, so that the front of the inner room is twenty cubits across (seven, six and seven). Others read the seven cubits as the depth of the doorway. The Hebrew is brief.

decisions.choice: into the inner room (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he went inside". Verse 4 shows that this is the inner room.

records.source: וַיָּ֨מָד אֶת־אָרְכּ֜וֹ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים אַמָּ֗ה וְרֹ֛חַב עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אַמָּ֖ה אֶל־פְּנֵ֣י הַֽהֵיכָ֑ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֖ה קֹ֥דֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And he measured its length, twenty cubits, and breadth twenty cubits, to [the] face of the temple; and he said to me, This [is] [the] holy of holies.
pieces: He measured the room beyond the main hall: it was {{units:about 35 feet|twenty cubits}} long and {{units:about 35 feet|twenty cubits}} wide. He said to me, "This is the most holy place."

L.4: And he measured its length, twenty cubits, and the width, twenty cubits, in front of the hall; and he said to me, "This [is] the holy of holies."

R.4: He measured the room at the far end of the main room. It was {{units:about 35 feet|twenty cubits}} long and {{units:about 35 feet|twenty cubits}} wide. He said to me, "This is the most holy place."

decisions.choice: the holy of holies: the most holy place, where the LORD's presence dwells
decisions.reason: The phrase means "the holiest place". In the tabernacle and in Solomon's temple it held the ark of the covenant beneath the cherubim (Exodus 26:33-34; 1 Kings 8:6). Ezekiel's temple names no ark; the LORD's glory itself fills the house (43:5). Hebrews 9:3-12 speaks of this room.

decisions.choice: twenty cubits by twenty: a perfect square, as in Solomon's temple
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 6:20 gives the inner room of Solomon's temple the same measures, a cube twenty cubits on every side.

decisions.choice: the holy of holies (L); the most holy place (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 6:16.

records.source: וַיָּ֥מָד קִֽיר־הַבַּ֖יִת שֵׁ֣שׁ אַמּ֑וֹת וְרֹ֣חַב הַצֵּלָע֩ אַרְבַּ֨ע אַמּ֜וֹת סָבִ֧יב׀סָבִ֛יב לַבַּ֖יִת סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And he measured [the] wall of the house, six cubits, and [the] breadth of the side chamber four cubits all around all around the house all around.
pieces: Then he measured the wall of the temple: it was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|six cubits}} thick. The side rooms all around the temple were each {{units:about 7 feet|four cubits}} wide.

L.5: And he measured the wall of the house, six cubits [thick], and the width of the side chamber, four cubits, all around the house on every side.

R.5: Then he measured the wall of the temple. It was {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|six cubits}} thick. Along the outside of the wall, all around the temple, there were side rooms. Each was {{units:about 7 feet|four cubits}} wide.

decisions.choice: side chamber: one of the small rooms built against the outside of the temple walls
decisions.reason: The word means "rib" or "side". 1 Kings 6:5-8 uses it for the rooms in several stories built around Solomon's temple, used for storage.

decisions.choice: side chamber (L); side rooms (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 6:5. The same English is used through the chapter.

records.source: וְהַצְּלָעוֹת֩ צֵלָ֨ע אֶל־צֵלָ֜ע שָׁל֧וֹשׁ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים פְּעָמִ֗ים וּ֠בָאוֹת בַּקִּ֨יר אֲשֶׁר־לַבַּ֧יִת לַצְּלָע֛וֹת סָבִ֥יב׀סָבִ֖יב לִהְי֣וֹת אֲחוּזִ֑ים וְלֹֽא־יִהְי֥וּ אֲחוּזִ֖ים בְּקִ֥יר הַבָּֽיִת׃
records.gloss: And the side chambers, side chamber on side chamber, three and thirty times; and [there were] going in in the wall which [was] to the house for the side chambers all around all around, to be supports, and not to be supports in [the] wall of the house.
pieces: The side rooms were in three stories, one above another, thirty on each story. The wall of the temple had ledges all around to hold up the side rooms, so that their beams did not have to be set into the wall of the temple itself.

L.6: And the side chambers [were] side chamber above side chamber, three [stories], and thirty in each story; and [there were ledges] going into the wall that [belonged] to the house for the side chambers all around, to be supports, so that they would not be supported in the wall of the house.

R.6: The side rooms were built in three levels, one on top of another. There were thirty rooms on each level. The temple wall had ledges all around it to hold up the side rooms. So the beams of the side rooms did not have to be fixed into the temple wall itself.

decisions.choice: three and thirty times: three stories with thirty rooms in each
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "three and thirty times" is usually read as three stories of thirty rooms. The Septuagint reads "thirty-three" twice, and some take the phrase as thirty-three rooms in all.

decisions.choice: going into the wall ... supports: ledges in the temple wall held the beams of the side rooms
decisions.reason: As in Solomon's temple (1 Kings 6:6), the wall of the temple was stepped back at each story, and the beams of the side rooms rested on the steps. The beams did not go into the temple wall itself, so the wall of the holy house was not pierced.

decisions.choice: [ledges] (L); ledges (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "going in". The sense is given by 1 Kings 6:6 (m2).

records.source: וְֽרָחֲבָ֡ה וְֽנָסְבָה֩ לְמַ֨עְלָה לְמַ֜עְלָה לַצְּלָע֗וֹת כִּ֣י מֽוּסַב־הַ֠בַּיִת לְמַ֨עְלָה לְמַ֜עְלָה סָבִ֤יב׀סָבִיב֙ לַבַּ֔יִת עַל־כֵּ֥ן רֹֽחַב־לַבַּ֖יִת לְמָ֑עְלָה וְכֵ֧ן הַתַּחְתּוֹנָ֛ה יַעֲלֶ֥ה עַל־הָעֶלְיוֹנָ֖ה לַתִּיכוֹנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was broader and wound around higher and higher to the side chambers, for [the] surrounding of the house [went] higher and higher all around all around the house; therefore [the] breadth of the house [increased] upward, and so from the lowest one went up to the highest by the middle.
pieces: The side rooms became wider at each story going up, because the structure surrounding the temple went up in stages all around it. So the building became wider toward the top, and one went up from the lowest story to the top story through the middle one.

L.7: And it became broader as it wound around higher and higher for the side chambers, for the surrounding [structure] of the house [went] higher and higher all around the house; so the breadth of the house [grew] upward, and thus from the lowest [story] one went up to the highest by the middle [one].

R.7: The side rooms got wider at each level going up, because the temple wall became thinner at each level. So the building was wider at the top. A stairway led from the bottom level through the middle level to the top level.

decisions.choice: the rooms widened with each story: the verse is hard and its details uncertain
alternatives: a winding stair led up to the side rooms
decisions.reason: The verse is very hard to construe. The likely sense, from 1 Kings 6:6, is that the temple wall stepped back at each story, so that the side rooms became wider at each level, and that there was a stairway or ramp from the lowest to the top story. Some read "wound around" as a winding stair (as 1 Kings 6:8). The translation keeps the general sense and does not settle the details.

decisions.choice: the temple wall became thinner at each level (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives the reason for the widening from 1 Kings 6:6 (m1).

records.source: וְרָאִ֧יתִי לַבַּ֛יִת גֹּ֖בַהּ סָבִ֣יב׀סָבִ֑יב מוּסְד֤וֹת הַצְּלָעוֹת֙ מְל֣וֹ הַקָּנֶ֔ה שֵׁ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת אַצִּֽילָה׃
records.gloss: And I saw to the house a height all around all around; [the] foundations of the side chambers [were] [the] fullness of the reed, six cubits to the joint.
pieces: I saw that the temple had a raised platform all around it. The foundations of the side rooms were a full reed, {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|six cubits}}, to the joint.

L.8: And I saw that the house [had] a raised platform all around; the foundations of the side chambers [were] a full reed, six cubits, to the joint.

R.8: I saw that the temple stood on a raised platform that went all the way around it. The foundations of the side rooms were {{units:about 10 1/2 feet|a reed}} high.

decisions.choice: a height: a raised platform or terrace on which the temple stood
decisions.reason: The word means "height". It is taken to be the base on which the temple and its side rooms stood, six cubits high, so that the house was raised above the inner court.

decisions.choice: to the joint: a hard word, perhaps the corner or edge of the platform
decisions.reason: The word is found only here and in 13:18, where it seems to mean "wrist" or "joint". Here it may mean the edge or corner of the platform. The sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: the foundations were a reed high (R)
decisions.reason: Readable leaves the hard last word (m2) unrendered and gives the measure.

records.source: רֹ֣חַב הַקִּ֧יר אֲֽשֶׁר־לַצֵּלָ֛ע אֶל־הַח֖וּץ חָמֵ֣שׁ אַמּ֑וֹת וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מֻנָּ֔ח בֵּ֥ית צְלָע֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר לַבָּֽיִת׃
records.gloss: [The] breadth of the wall which [belonged] to the side chamber to the outside [was] five cubits; and what [was] left free between [the] side chambers which [belonged] to the house.
pieces: The outer wall of the side rooms was {{units:about 8 3/4 feet|five cubits}} thick. There was an open space between the side rooms of the temple

L.9: The thickness of the outer wall of the side chambers [was] five cubits; and [there was] a free space between the side chambers of the house

R.9: The outside wall of the side rooms was {{units:about 8 3/4 feet|five cubits}} thick. There was an open area around the side rooms of the temple,

decisions.choice: what was left free: an open space or terrace left around the building
decisions.reason: The word means "what is left" or "set down". It names an open strip on the platform outside the side rooms (verse 11). Some take the verse to end "between the side rooms of the house and the rooms" with verse 10.

records.source: וּבֵ֨ין הַלְּשָׁכ֜וֹת רֹ֣חַב עֶשְׂרִ֥ים אַמָּ֛ה סָבִ֥יב לַבַּ֖יִת סָבִ֥יב׀סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And between the rooms [the] breadth [was] twenty cubits around the house all around all around.
pieces: and the rooms; it was {{units:about 35 feet|twenty cubits}} wide all around the temple.

L.10: and the chambers, a width of twenty cubits, all around the house on every side.

R.10: and beyond it, between the temple and the other rooms, was a space {{units:about 35 feet|twenty cubits}} wide all around the temple.

decisions.choice: between the rooms: the open space between the temple building and the priests' rooms
decisions.reason: "The rooms" here are not the side rooms of verse 5 but the rooms of the priests in the inner court, described in 42:1-14. A space of twenty cubits separated them from the temple building.

decisions.choice: verses 9 and 10 read as one sentence (all levels)
decisions.reason: The end of verse 9 and verse 10 form one statement about the open space, so every level runs verse 9 into verse 10.

records.source: וּפֶ֤תַח הַצֵּלָע֙ לַמֻּנָּ֔ח פֶּ֤תַח אֶחָד֙ דֶּ֣רֶךְ הַצָּפ֔וֹן וּפֶ֥תַח אֶחָ֖ד לַדָּר֑וֹם וְרֹ֨חַב֙ מְק֣וֹם הַמֻּנָּ֔ח חָמֵ֥שׁ אַמּ֖וֹת סָבִ֥יב׀סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And [the] entrance of the side chamber [was] to the free space, one entrance [the] way of the north and one entrance to the south; and [the] breadth of the place of the free space [was] five cubits all around all around.
pieces: The side rooms had doors opening onto the open space, one door on the north side and one on the south. The open space was {{units:about 8 3/4 feet|five cubits}} wide all around.

L.11: And the entrances of the side chambers [opened] onto the free space, one entrance toward the north and one entrance toward the south; and the width of the free space [was] five cubits all around.

R.11: The side rooms had doorways that opened onto the open area. One doorway was on the north side, and one was on the south side. The open area was {{units:about 8 3/4 feet|five cubits}} wide all around.

records.source: וְהַבִּנְיָ֡ן אֲשֶׁר֩ אֶל־פְּנֵ֨י הַגִּזְרָ֜ה פְּאַ֣ת דֶּֽרֶךְ־הַיָּ֗ם רֹ֚חַב שִׁבְעִ֣ים אַמָּ֔ה וְקִ֧יר הַבִּנְיָ֛ן חָֽמֵשׁ־אַמּ֥וֹת רֹ֖חַב סָבִ֣יב׀סָבִ֑יב וְאָרְכּ֖וֹ תִּשְׁעִ֥ים אַמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And the building which [was] to [the] face of the separate area, [the] side of [the] way of the sea, [the] breadth seventy cubits, and [the] wall of the building five cubits breadth all around all around, and its length ninety cubits.
pieces: The building facing the separate area on the west side was {{units:about 122 1/2 feet|seventy cubits}} wide. Its wall was {{units:about 8 3/4 feet|five cubits}} thick all around, and it was {{units:about 157 1/2 feet|ninety cubits}} long.

L.12: And the building that [was] facing the separate area on the side toward the west [was] seventy cubits in breadth; and the building's wall, five cubits thick all around; and its length, ninety cubits.

R.12: At the west end, behind the temple, there was a separate area with a building facing it. The building was {{units:about 122 1/2 feet|seventy cubits}} wide and {{units:about 157 1/2 feet|ninety cubits}} long. Its walls were {{units:about 8 3/4 feet|five cubits}} thick all around.

decisions.choice: the separate area: an area set apart behind the temple
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning "cut off". It names the area behind the temple building on the west, set apart from the rest of the courts (verses 13-15; 42:1, 10, 13). Whether it is an open yard or a building plot is not certain.

decisions.choice: the way of the sea: west
decisions.reason: Israel's sea, the Mediterranean, lies to the west, so "toward the sea" means "toward the west".

decisions.choice: the building: a large building of unknown use behind the temple
decisions.reason: The text does not say what the building on the west was for. It may have been for storage or for the temple's service; 2 Kings 23:11 and 1 Chronicles 26:18 speak of a structure on the west side of Solomon's temple.

decisions.choice: the separate area (all levels)
decisions.reason: The same English is used for this word through chapters 41-42.

records.source: וּמָדַ֣ד אֶת־הַבַּ֔יִת אֹ֖רֶךְ מֵאָ֣ה אַמָּ֑ה וְהַגִּזְרָ֤ה וְהַבִּנְיָה֙ וְקִ֣ירוֹתֶ֔יהָ אֹ֖רֶךְ מֵאָ֥ה אַמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And he measured the house, length a hundred cubits, and the separate area and the building and its walls, length a hundred cubits.
pieces: Then he measured the temple: it was {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}} long. The separate area with the building and its walls was also {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}} long.

L.13: And he measured the house, a hundred cubits long; and the separate area and the building with its walls, a hundred cubits long.

R.13: Then he measured the temple. It was {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}} long. The separate area, with the building and its walls, was also {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}} long.

decisions.choice: a hundred cubits: the temple and its surroundings are laid out in squares of a hundred cubits
decisions.reason: The temple building is a hundred cubits long, and the inner court and the area behind the temple are each a hundred cubits square (40:47; verse 14). The repeated hundred stresses order and completeness.

records.source: וְרֹחַב֩ פְּנֵ֨י הַבַּ֧יִת וְהַגִּזְרָ֛ה לַקָּדִ֖ים מֵאָ֥ה אַמָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] breadth of [the] face of the house and the separate area to the east [was] a hundred cubits.
pieces: The width of the temple's front, together with the separate area, on the east side was {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}}.

L.14: And the width of the front of the house and of the separate area toward the east [was] a hundred cubits.

R.14: The front of the temple on the east side, together with the separate areas beside it, was {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}} wide.

records.source: וּמָדַ֣ד אֹֽרֶךְ־הַ֠בִּנְיָן אֶל־פְּנֵ֨י הַגִּזְרָ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר עַל־אַחֲרֶ֧יהָ וְאַתִּיקֶ֛יהָא מִפּ֥וֹ וּמִפּ֖וֹ מֵאָ֣ה אַמָּ֑ה וְהַֽהֵיכָל֙ הַפְּנִימִ֔י וְאֻֽלַמֵּ֖י הֶחָצֵֽר׃
records.gloss: And he measured [the] length of the building to [the] face of the separate area which [was] behind it, and its galleries from here and from here, a hundred cubits; and the temple the inner and [the] porches of the court.
pieces: He measured the length of the building facing the separate area at the back of the temple, with its galleries on each side: it was {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}}. The main hall, the inner room and the porch facing the court

L.15: And he measured the length of the building facing the separate area at the back of it, with its galleries on the one side and on the other: a hundred cubits; and the inner hall and the porches of the court

R.15: He measured the length of the building that faced the separate area behind the temple, with its galleries on each side. It was {{units:about 175 feet|100 cubits}}. The main room, the inner room, and the porch facing the courtyard

decisions.choice: galleries: a hard word, perhaps terraces, balconies or passages
decisions.reason: The word is found only in Ezekiel (here, verse 16 and 42:3, 5). It seems to name a structure that stepped back in stages, such as terraced balconies or galleries. The exact sense is unknown.

decisions.choice: the inner hall and the porches of the court: the sentence runs on into verse 16
decisions.reason: The end of the verse begins a list of the parts of the temple that were paneled, which continues in verse 16. "The inner hall" may be the main hall and the inner room together. The Hebrew is very compressed.

decisions.choice: galleries (all levels)
decisions.reason: The same English is used for this word in verse 16 and 42:3, 5.

records.source: הַסִּפִּ֡ים וְהַחַלּוֹנִ֣ים הָ֠אֲטֻמוֹת וְהָאַתִּיקִ֤ים׀סָבִיב֙ לִשְׁלָשְׁתָּ֔ם נֶ֧גֶד הַסַּ֛ף שְׂחִ֥יף עֵ֖ץ סָבִ֣יב׀סָבִ֑יב וְהָאָ֨רֶץ֙ עַד־הַֽחַלֹּנ֔וֹת וְהַֽחַלֹּנ֖וֹת מְכֻסּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: the thresholds and the closed windows and the galleries all around to [the] three of them opposite the threshold [were] paneled with wood all around all around, and from the ground to the windows, and the windows [were] covered,
pieces: the thresholds, the recessed windows, and the galleries around all three of them were paneled with wood all around, from the floor up to the windows. The windows were covered,

L.16: the thresholds, the recessed windows and the galleries all around the three of them, opposite the threshold, [were] paneled with wood all around, from the ground to the windows; and the windows [were] covered,

R.16: the doorways, the windows set deep in their frames, and the galleries around all three of them were covered with wood paneling all around, from the floor up to the windows. The windows were covered too.

decisions.choice: paneled with wood: covered with wooden boards
decisions.reason: The word is rare. Solomon's temple too was lined with cedar boards on the inside, from the floor to the ceiling (1 Kings 6:15).

decisions.choice: the windows were covered: perhaps with lattice work or with panels
decisions.reason: The word means "covered". The windows may have been covered with lattices, or the paneling may have run up to and around them. It is not certain.

decisions.choice: recessed windows (L, B); windows set deep in their frames (R)
decisions.reason: As in 40:16.

records.source: עַל־מֵעַ֣ל הַפֶּ֡תַח וְעַד־הַבַּיִת֩ הַפְּנִימִ֨י וְלַח֜וּץ וְאֶל־כָּל־הַקִּ֨יר סָבִ֧יב׀סָבִ֛יב בַּפְּנִימִ֥י וּבַחִיצ֖וֹן מִדּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: to over the entrance and to the inner house and to the outside, and on all the wall all around all around, in the inner and in the outer, [by] measurements.
pieces: even the space above the entrance into the inner room and outside it. On all the walls all around, both inside and outside, there were measured panels,

L.17: to the space above the entrance, both into the inner room and outside, and on all the walls all around, inside and outside, by measure.

R.17: The paneling went above the doorway into the inner room, and on the outside too. All the walls all around, inside and outside, were covered with panels of the same size,

decisions.choice: measurements: perhaps panels of fixed size, or simply "measured"
alternatives: the carvings were laid out by measure
decisions.reason: The last word, "measurements", may mean that the walls were divided into panels of fixed size, or that the guide measured them too. Some think it introduces the carvings of verse 18.

decisions.choice: measured panels (B); panels of the same size (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take the word as describing the paneling (m1).

records.source: וְעָשׂ֥וּי כְּרוּבִ֖ים וְתִֽמֹרִ֑ים וְתִֽמֹרָה֙ בֵּין־כְּר֣וּב לִכְר֔וּב וּשְׁנַ֥יִם פָּנִ֖ים לַכְּרֽוּב׃
records.gloss: And [it was] made [with] cherubim and palm trees, and a palm tree between cherub and cherub, and two faces to [each] cherub,
pieces: carved with cherubim and palm trees, with a palm tree between each pair of cherubim. Each cherub had two faces:

L.18: and [it was] made with cherubim and palm trees, with a palm tree between cherub and cherub; and each cherub [had] two faces:

R.18: carved with cherubim and palm trees. There was a palm tree between every two cherubim. Each cherub had two faces.

decisions.choice: cherubim and palm trees: the garden of God
decisions.reason: Solomon's temple too was carved with cherubim, palm trees and open flowers (1 Kings 6:29). Together they picture a garden guarded by cherubim, as Eden was (Genesis 3:24; Ezekiel 28:13-14).

decisions.choice: two faces: a human face and a lion's face
decisions.reason: The cherubim of chapters 1 and 10 have four faces each (1:10; 10:14). These carved cherubim show two faces, probably because a carving on a flat wall shows only two sides, one turned to each palm tree.

decisions.choice: cherubim (all levels)
decisions.reason: As in chapter 10.

records.source: וּפְנֵ֨י אָדָ֤ם אֶל־הַתִּֽמֹרָה֙ מִפּ֔וֹ וּפְנֵֽי־כְפִ֥יר אֶל־הַתִּֽמֹרָ֖ה מִפּ֑וֹ עָשׂ֥וּי אֶל־כָּל־הַבַּ֖יִת סָבִ֥יב׀סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: and [the] face of a human toward the palm tree from here, and [the] face of a young lion toward the palm tree from here; made on all the house all around all around.
pieces: a human face turned toward the palm tree on one side, and a lion's face turned toward the palm tree on the other. They were carved all around the whole temple.

L.19: the face of a human being toward the palm tree here, and the face of a young lion toward the palm tree there; [they were] made on the whole house all around.

R.19: a human face turned toward the palm tree on one side, and a lion's face turned toward the palm tree on the other side. These were carved all around the whole temple.

records.source: מֵהָאָ֨רֶץ֙ עַד־מֵעַ֣ל הַפֶּ֔תַח הַכְּרוּבִ֥ים וְהַתִּֽמֹרִ֖ים עֲשׂוּיִ֑ם וְקִ֖יר הַׄהֵׄיׄכָֽׄלׄ׃
records.gloss: From the ground to over the entrance, the cherubim and the palm trees [were] made, and [on] [the] wall of the temple.
pieces: From the floor to above the entrance, cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall of the main hall.

L.20: From the ground to above the entrance the cherubim and the palm trees [were] made, and [on] the wall of the hall.

R.20: Cherubim and palm trees were carved on the walls of the main room, from the floor up to above the doorway.

decisions.choice: and the wall of the temple: a phrase standing apart at the end
decisions.reason: The last words sit loosely in the sentence. They may mean "on the wall of the hall", or they may begin the next verse. The translation takes them with this verse.

records.source: הַֽהֵיכָ֖ל מְזוּזַ֣ת רְבֻעָ֑ה וּפְנֵ֣י הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ הַמַּרְאֶ֖ה כַּמַּרְאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: The temple: doorpost square; and [the] face of the holy place, the appearance like the appearance.
pieces: The doorframes of the main hall were square, and the front of the most holy place looked the same.

L.21: The hall [had] square doorposts; and [as for] the front of the holy place, the appearance [was] like the appearance [of the other].

R.21: The doorframes of the main room were square. The front of the most holy place looked the same.

decisions.choice: doorpost square ... the appearance like the appearance: a terse and difficult verse
alternatives: the front of the holy place had the appearance of an altar, joined to verse 22
decisions.reason: The words are very brief. They seem to say that the doorframes of the main hall were square, or rectangular, and that the entrance to the most holy place looked like it. "The holy place" here is probably the inner room, as in verse 23. The Septuagint takes the last words with verse 22.

records.source: הַמִּזְבֵּ֡חַ עֵ֣ץ שָׁלוֹשׁ֩ אַמּ֨וֹת גָּבֹ֜הַּ וְאָרְכּ֣וֹ שְׁתַּֽיִם־אַמּ֗וֹת וּמִקְצֹֽעוֹתָיו֙ ל֔וֹ וְאָרְכּ֥וֹ וְקִֽירֹתָ֖יו עֵ֑ץ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֚ה הַשֻּׁלְחָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: The altar [was] wood, three cubits high, and its length two cubits; and its corners [were] to it, and its length and its sides [were] wood. And he spoke to me, This [is] the table which [is] before Yahweh.
pieces: There was an altar of wood {{units:about 5 1/4 feet|three cubits}} high and {{units:about 3 1/2 feet|two cubits}} long. Its corners, its length and its sides were wooden. He said to me, "This is the table that stands before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

L.22: The altar, wood, three cubits high, and its length, two cubits; and it [had] its corners, and its length and its sides [were] of wood. And he said to me, "This [is] the table that [is] before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

R.22: There was a wooden altar {{units:about 5 1/4 feet|three cubits}} high and {{units:about 3 1/2 feet|two cubits}} long. Its corners and its sides, all along its length, were made of wood. The man said to me, "This is the table that stands in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."

decisions.choice: a wooden altar, the table before the LORD: probably the table of the bread of the Presence
decisions.reason: In the tabernacle and in Solomon's temple the main hall held the table for the bread of the Presence and the golden incense altar (Exodus 25:23-30; 30:1-6; 1 Kings 7:48). Here a single wooden "altar" is called "the table that is before the LORD". It is usually taken as the table for the bread of the Presence, which held offerings before the LORD; some think of the incense altar. Malachi 1:7, 12 calls the altar "the table of the LORD".

decisions.choice: its length: perhaps to be read "its base", with the Septuagint
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "its length" a second time, which makes little sense in a list of parts. The Septuagint reads "its base", which differs by one letter. The translation keeps the Hebrew, perhaps meaning the long sides of the table.

decisions.choice: the man said (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, the guide of 40:3.

records.source: וּשְׁתַּ֧יִם דְּלָת֛וֹת לַֽהֵיכָ֖ל וְלַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And two doors [belonged] to the temple and to the holy place.
pieces: The main hall and the most holy place each had a double door.

L.23: And the hall and the holy place [each] had two doors.

R.23: The main room and the most holy place each had a double door.

decisions.choice: two doors to the hall and to the holy place: a double door at each entrance
decisions.reason: Each of the two rooms had a doorway closed by a door in two leaves (verse 24), like the doors of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 6:31-35). "The holy place" is the inner room.

decisions.choice: the most holy place (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the holy place", meaning here the inner room (m1); Balanced and Readable say "most holy place" so that it is not taken for the main hall.

records.source: וּשְׁתַּ֥יִם דְּלָת֖וֹת לַדְּלָת֑וֹת שְׁ֚תַּיִם מוּסַבּ֣וֹת דְּלָת֔וֹת שְׁ֚תַּיִם לְדֶ֣לֶת אֶחָ֔ת וּשְׁתֵּ֥י דְלָת֖וֹת לָאַחֶֽרֶת׃
records.gloss: And two leaves [belonged] to the doors, two turning leaves; two to one door, and two leaves to the other.
pieces: Each door had two leaves that swung on hinges, two leaves for each door.

L.24: And the doors [had] two leaves, two leaves that turned: two for one door, and two leaves for the other [door].

R.24: Each door had two parts that could fold back, two parts for each door.

decisions.choice: two turning leaves: folding or swinging leaves
decisions.reason: Each door was made of two leaves that turned or folded, as in Solomon's temple, where each leaf was itself in two folding parts (1 Kings 6:34).

records.source: וַעֲשׂוּיָ֨ה אֲלֵיהֶ֜ן אֶל־דַּלְת֤וֹת הַֽהֵיכָל֙ כְּרוּבִ֣ים וְתִֽמֹרִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲשׂוּיִ֖ם לַקִּיר֑וֹת וְעָ֥ב עֵ֛ץ אֶל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאוּלָ֖ם מֵהַחֽוּץ׃
records.gloss: And made on them, on [the] doors of the temple, [were] cherubim and palm trees, as [they were] made for the walls; and a canopy of wood [was] on [the] face of the porch from the outside.
pieces: On the doors of the main hall were carved cherubim and palm trees like those on the walls, and there was a wooden canopy over the front of the porch outside.

L.25: And on them, on the doors of the hall, cherubim and palm trees [were] made, as [they were] made on the walls; and [there was] a canopy of wood on the front of the porch outside.

R.25: On the doors of the main room there were carvings of cherubim and palm trees, like those on the walls. Outside, over the front of the porch, there was a wooden roof.

decisions.choice: a canopy: an overhanging roof or threshold of wood
decisions.reason: The word is rare (also verse 26 and 1 Kings 7:6). It seems to mean a projecting roof or canopy, though some take it as a wooden threshold or step.

records.source: וְחַלּוֹנִ֨ים אֲטֻמ֤וֹת וְתִֽמֹרִים֙ מִפּ֣וֹ וּמִפּ֔וֹ אֶל־כִּתְפ֖וֹת הָֽאוּלָ֑ם וְצַלְע֥וֹת הַבַּ֖יִת וְהָעֻבִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And closed windows and palm trees from here and from here to [the] sides of the porch, and [the] side chambers of the house and the canopies.
pieces: There were recessed windows and palm trees on both sides of the porch, and on the side rooms of the temple and the canopies.

L.26: And [there were] recessed windows and palm trees here and there, on the sides of the porch; [so also] the side chambers of the house and the canopies.

R.26: There were windows set deep in their frames, and carved palm trees, on both sides of the porch. The side rooms of the temple and the roofs over them were decorated the same way.

decisions.choice: and the side chambers of the house and the canopies: a closing list
decisions.reason: The last words are a bare list. They may mean that the side rooms and canopies were decorated in the same way, or simply that they were part of the building described. The account of the temple building ends here.

decisions.choice: recessed windows (L, B); windows set deep in their frames (R)
decisions.reason: As in 40:16.
